<template>` emulates one existing host template — its `initialize` identity, advertised capabilities, protocol versions and tool v
isibility, plus its model settings where the suite does not set them. It never launches the real client, and reports say \"emulate
d\". The suite's model, and any authored `systemPrompt` / `temperature`, win over the template's. `target.hosts` in the file is re

## Reasoning effort

A local suit
e file does **not** take a reasoning effort yet: `defaults` has no\n`reasoningEffort` key (a dialect-2 default needs a matching ba
ckend field on the\nsuite's default config, which has not shipped), so the value is rejected as an\nunknown key rather than accept

ed and ignored. Ways to run a local suite at an
effort today:

* Run it against a **saved client** with `runWithClient`: the cl
ient's hosted\n model selection carries `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the runner applies it\n (and refuses a model that cannot
) — see [`HostRunner`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/host-runner#reasoningeffort).\n* Build the runner yourself with `Host
Runner({ reasoningEffort })`.\n* Set the effort on the hosted suite's model selection with\n `mcpjam cloud eval update --effort <

level>` (see the [CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#reasoning-effort)).

## Tool policy

A suite's `defa
ults.toolPolicy` is enforced before the MCP call: a denied tool never reaches the server, the model receives the refusal, and the
report records the block by case, iteration and call id. A blocked call is not graded as a call and is not an executed tool span.
A `deny` name that matches no tool the servers expose is invalid input (exit `2`); an unmatched `allow` is a warning. With no `too

lPolicy`, nothing is restrained.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For the upcoming Inspector eval runner with MCP App view tools enabled, use `v
iew:<name>` in a suite's `toolPolicy.allow` or `deny`, for example `view:make_move`. These names wait until the app renders; plain
tool names keep the validation described above. Assertions and side-effect manifests still use `make_move`. This syntax does not

enable view tools in the local SDK suite-file runner.

## Imported cases

Native and claimed-`exact` imported cases run with n
jam test .mcpjam/evals/imported.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reason \"Reviewed against the up

stream rubric"
```

`unsupported` and `unresolved` cases never run. Approving a native, `exact`, disabled, unselected or unkno

wn case is refused. A local approval is recorded as local evidence; it claims no hosted approver.

## What runs locally

| Cap

ability | Local behavior |
| - | - |
| Prompt steps (including several per case) | Run as one conversation per iteration |
| De
terministic assertions (steps and `assertions`) | Graded with the hosted assertion engine |\n| Direct `toolCall` steps | Refused b
efore anything runs — use a prompt, or run hosted |\n| `interact` steps, widget/render and tool-discovery assertions | Refused bef
ore anything runs |\n| Gating assertions on tool results or per-call latency (`toolResultContains`, `toolResultMatches`, `toolResu
ltMatchesSchema`, `toolResultSizeUnder`, `toolLatencyUnder`) | Refused before anything runs — a local run does not capture tool re
sults or timings yet. An advisory one is reported as not measured |\n| An enabled gating or required judge | Refused before anythi
ng runs |\n| An advisory judge (including the hosted default) | Not run; the report says so |\n| `suppressedSuiteStandardCheckIds`
| Refused — a local run has no suite-standard registry |\n\nEvery selected case is checked before any model or tool call, so an u

nsupported later case costs nothing. Hosted-only capabilities run with `mcpjam cloud eval run --file <file>`.

## Output

* Wi
th `--format human` (the default on a terminal), a summary: the verdict, each case's gradeable-iteration count against its thresho
ld, failing assertions, not-measured iterations, policy blocks and un-run judges.\n* With `--format json` (the default when stdout
is not a terminal: a pipe, a CI log, or an agent's shell), one JSON report on stdout (`kind: \"eval-local-run\"`). Pass `--format
human` to get the summary there instead.\n* `--reporter json-summary|junit-xml|html` writes that document to stdout; the human su
mmary and progress go to stderr.\n* `--out <path>` writes the report atomically (in the `--reporter` format, else JSON) and prints
the path.\n\nEvery report identifies the run as local and emulated, carries the source-file sha256, the per-case evaluator hashes
, the selection, the effective model and rail per case and each server's binding source, and states that upload was off. Server he
aders, environment objects, command lines and token-bearing URLs never appear in any output, and every credential the run was give
n is redacted wherever observed text (an error, a tool argument) repeats it.\n\nThe unit of a verdict is the **case**; iterations
are evidence. A JUnit consumer receives a `<failure>` only for a measured failure — provider errors, evaluator errors and interrup

ted work are reported as skipped, never as failed assertions.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | The run c
ompleted and its decision passed |\n| `1` | The run completed and its decision failed — the only source of `1` |\n| `2` | Invalid
file or flags, an unsupported local capability, an import/approval refusal, or an invalid tool-policy deny name |\n| `3` | Missing
or rejected model or platform credentials, including during execution |\n| `4` | Setup, connection, tool catalog, binding, interp
olation or billing failure, or a report that could not be written |\n| `5` | Inconclusive, interrupted, an integrity failure, or n
o complete verdict |\n\n`Ctrl-C` stops the run cooperatively: completed evidence is kept, the report is written, and the command e
xits `5` — an interrupted run is never presented as a completed release gate. A second `Ctrl-C` exits immediately.\n\n## From code
\n\nThe same engine is `runSuiteFile` in `@mcpjam/sdk`. It takes explicit bindings and credentials — it reads no files, environmen
t or login store — and returns the decision and the report. See [runSuiteFile](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/run-suite-fil

e.md).
